formalObservation.Composition:
The work is dominated by a long horizontal arrangement of interconnected figure-like structures.

Three major upper forms:

1. smaller rounded figure toward the left
2. large elongated central figure
3. smaller vertically oriented figure toward the right

A long continuous lower structure runs beneath them.
formalObservation.Primary Forms:
Left figure:

- horizontally elongated form
- circular eye-like marking
- another small interior circular marking
- projecting upper element
- broad lower section
- sequence of rounded forms beneath

Central figure:

- largest form
- prominent circular eye
- elongated head/body contour
- projecting front structure
- open mouth
- triangular tooth-like marks
- long lower extension

Right figure:

- vertically oriented oval/rounded figure
- prominent circular eye
- open mouth
- triangular tooth-like marks
- elongated lower body
formalObservation.Secondary Forms:
Long irregular horizontally extended lower-middle structure consisting of:

- multiple rounded segments
- irregular contours
- parallel hatching
- dark lower edge

A separate thin horizontal line appears below it.
formalObservation.Structural Forms:
- Long horizontal body/ground
- Rounded segmented forms
- Horizontal connecting structures
- Vertical / curved supports
- Repeated oval forms
formalObservation.Repeated Forms:
- Circular eyes
- Rounded segments
- Triangular tooth marks
- Parallel hatching
- Horizontal bands
formalObservation.Mark-Making:
Heavy horizontal hatching, with:

- dense vertical hatching
- broad contouring
- darker filled regions
- repeated short strokes
- lighter internal construction marks

The central figure is particularly strongly defined by repeated directional hatching around its contour.
formalObservation.Formal Language:
- Strong horizontal axis.
- Three principal figure-like units.
- One dominant central figure.
- Repeated circular and triangular motifs.
- Lower segmented structure functions as a secondary visual layer.
- Organic contours dominate, but geometric simplification remains present.
- Hatching creates surface continuity across separate forms.
